caseName: He Had a Date to Leave Me
title: Adrienne & Ross

questions.text: Thank you for doing this. I'm not going to fall apart, I promise... could you start with the last person who wrote to him? A name is enough.
questions.hint: Take a look in the Messages app, there must be someone who sent him a message recently.

questions.text: That's not a name I've ever heard in this apartment. Sorry to be difficult — can you get me her surname too? I want to know who she is.
questions.hint: If he saved this mysterious correspondent, her full identity must be in his Contacts directory.

questions.text: Kendra Vaughn. I've said it out loud twice now and it still means nothing to me. How long has she been in his phone? In months, please.
questions.hint: Open his conversation with Kendra in Messages and scroll back - he says exactly how long they've been together.

questions.text: Four months. Right under my nose... does he have a name for her, a soft one? I know how that sounds. Tell me the word anyway.
questions.hint: Open his main messaging and browse through their daily exchanges. Among the affectionate messages, a sweet word comes up very regularly.

questions.text: Birdie. He calls me Adri, and that's about as far as it goes... can you tell me how often they were seeing each other? The pattern, please.
questions.hint: If they meet regularly in secret, these precious moments are surely disguised under a fake professional name in his Calendar.

questions.text: Every week. Written down like an appointment... somebody has been backing that story up for him, I'm sure of it. Which of his friends is it?
questions.hint: One of his close friends must be in on it to serve as his alibi. Explore his recent WhatsApp discussions to find who's covering for him.

questions.text: A room, two nights. He paid for that and then came home and asked me how my day was... which hotel is it?
questions.hint: Booking confirmations are often sent by email. Even if he tried to cover his tracks, look in the trash of his Email inbox.

onboarding.text: Hey... I'm Adrienne. I've written this out twice already and deleted it twice. I'm not going to cry on you. I did all of that a few weeks ago.
onboarding.label: Adrienne

onboarding.text: A year in the same apartment in Kansas City. He draws buildings for a living... he's better with brick than with people, and I loved that about him. I did.
onboarding.label: Adrienne & Ross

onboarding.text: Three weeks ago he started taking his calls out in the hallway. Phone face down on the table. If he goes out, it's a client... and I stopped believing that a while back.
onboarding.label: Ross

onboarding.text: He left before eight. A walkthrough at nine, he said. His phone is on my kitchen counter, face up. He's back by lunch... I want you to find nothing. I don't think you will.
onboarding.label: Adrienne

Ross, good evening
